description.en: Transjordan south of the Dead Sea around the castles of Kerak (Krak du Désert) and Montréal (Shawbak); the Franks reached Aylah (Aqaba).
description.ar: شرق الأردن جنوب البحر الميت حول قلعتي الكرك (كراك دي شيفالييه) ومونتريال (الشوبك)؛ وبلغ الفرنجة أيلة (العقبة).
description.he: עבר הירדן מדרום לים המלח סביב מצודות כרך (Krak du Désert) ומונריאל (שובק); הפרנקים הגיעו לאילה (עקבה).

sources.quote: Le Krak du Désert, a heavily fortified Crusader citadel, was built on the site of the ancient fortress in 1132; it fell to the Muslims in 1188
Reginald of Châtillon, lord of Kerak and Montréal, broke the truce with the Muslims by attacking a caravan.
Though the Franks did push southward to Aylah (or Elim, modern Al-ʿAqabah), all attempts to move eastward failed
after the lapse of the Turkish peril in 1115. In the fall of that year he built in the Transjordan the castle of ash-Shaubak, or Krak de Montréal
was controlled by three castles: Krak de Montréal (ash-Shaubak) built by Baldwin I in 1115
Kerak, founded in 1142 by Pagan le Bouteiller and enlarged by his immediate successors.
Hebron was separated from the royal domain in 1161 and made over to Philip de Milly together with the seigneurie of Transjordan.
